text: There've been really odd disappearances recently. Odder than usual. No signs of explosive mishap or anything. People have just... vanished, with only a slick of oil left behind.
Those old weather machines around the city are starting to malfunction. Doesn't really grind my gears, but I suspect the Overclockers will want them replaced.
Kummuuuu, who runs the emporium, apparently lost some prized machine of his a few weeks ago, and he's been really broken up about it.
You always get fabricants who submit their names for breeding, but then never come pick up their offspring. I hear it really steams up the High Foremer when that happens.
Folks are saying a  man without a head is wandering around the temple district. Poor f'lah, he'll never get ahead with that kind of behavior.
You ever been to the top of the clocktower? Me neither, but logically someone must have.
If you're pious, you might want to talk to the high priests, they've always got work.
Rumors? Are you mad? There's no time for such nonsense!

Entities and minds created by Sotha Sil to run and monitor his city. They are like gods in power, yet like children in thought. All mechanisms in the city are subject to them, and you have no doubt encountered several, even if you do not know it. You have met the Regent, as I understand it, and he is one of those Intelligences.
Hah, a skinny bugger like you wouldn't put a dent in my foil! Now piss off, fetcher, I've got customers to sell to.

Aight, aight! Seht. friend, you've got a short fuse on you. Every midnight, after I close up shop, there's a few robed figures near the south alleys. They hang out 'round the catacombs, they sell me the augmentations cheap.
I ain't telling you nothing.

Nope! Not what I'd consider imperfections, far from it even. Those who augment believe themselves closer to our god! But once you become fully machine, are you still really you? A question to be, hah, wondered! No, %PCName, I am not the seller you look for, but I know where he makes shop. In the Temple District, from 5 to 6 each night, he pawns his fake arms to the preachers and priests. Though I do not believe him responsible for the mess that poor district is in.

I'm afraid no priests or religious groups ever come in here. Not when we're all rivals in this city. If they did get augmentations, they'd have bought them secondhand from a merchant, probably a traveling one, like Alpharius, the clockseller. I believe he's taken up shop near your home, Fyr Manor, no?
It's what happens when you get a new arm, or a new leg. A better one usually, fully mechanical. Uran bought his recently from a mer selling his wares at the front of the district.

An outlander wanting augmentations? What an odd thing, development, or tale.
I cannot give you outward aumgentations, but if I adapted a few machines, hopefully this would allow you to gain enhancements, as we do.
The only question that remains, is what do you want augmented? Your strength, your speed, or your intelligence.

No, don't answer. It was a question that must be left to hang. Whatever your goals are, I can help you achieve them. Consider that I am a merchant. I trade things. But what I trade are artifacts of unimportance. Broken things that still might have a use. They're called 'imperfections'. A spoon-fork, a crossbow that fires backwards, a square gear: if you find things like this, bring them to me. I will trade your imperfections for my imperfections, and perhaps they may find a perfect use with their new owners

Oh no, sera, I don't mean the roaring monster that guards the Clockwork God's chambers, I mean these! Odd bits and bobs of the world that have trickled by merchant or motion into my care. What do they do? Sometimes I know, sometimes I don't. Such is life, full of certainty and equal uncertainty. Take yourself, for example. I hear from the whispers of the realm that you wish to save the city. But do you really know what you are doing? What you want to do? What you will do?

Save? Safe? Why? Who says the city needs saving? Who says saving is repairing? Who said saving is, in fact, saving? Not I, not me. If the city needs saving, it is from itself, and rightly so. You are an outlander, and the others of my kind are far too young; with my age comes memories of what the city once was.  No, it doesn't need to be fixed, or repaired, because it is not broken. It is merely an experiment that has reached its end.
The city you see before you did not come from his godhood, and his tinkering is the result of his own skill. Respect must be given to such ingenuity.

Seht, Sotha Sil, the Mystery of Morrowind, for he is such a mystery, even to his sons and daughters! Though mysterious not in origin, but in person. Born chi, should've been dwe, more alt than alt. Mystic, engineer, god, not really a god. We owe him our lives, though not his love. Don't think our King evil, %PCName, he serves a higher power, and that drives him above all else. At the same time, however, do not underestimate him.
Again, thank you for the publicity boost. Yes.

I know! I have seen people coming and going into my corners all the time! I think? They might just be lost. Yes.
Well, you've probably done some good regardless, have a reward! Yep.
Hm? Well I suppose I could, it wouldn't hurt after all.
Hm? Well I suppose I could, it wouldn't hurt after all.
Give those flyers to people who come into contact with other people. Yeah.

I've been so busy just inventing the things I haven't had time to spreading the word about things!
I think? I haven't eaten in days, and I think I'm starting to hallucinate. Are you really there? Yes? Good. Perhaps you could assist me by handing out these advertisement flyers to people who might spread them around to other people. Yes? You know, like tavern owners, community leaders, those people. Yes.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Residential District, Aroban's Sehtly Wonders
text: Yeah... I heard about that. It's got Miri shook up really bad.
Talk to some of my girls, see what they know, try and find the person who's been killing my workers.

I used to have some more girls, but lately, some... things have been happening. I always try to watch out for 'em, but someone has been murdering the poor things in their home, taking their arms and whatnot. People don't care much about strippers, but I, however, do. I'd like you to talk to them, and try and find out who is behind these murders, and stop 'em dead in their tracks.
I wish I could go home. Or just find a way to fit in.

Okay. Okay. Deep breaths. I can do this.
Sorry, I suppose ultimately I'm afraid of never going home. I wouldn't consider that too bad, but, I'm scared of these people. If I could never get home, I would be stuck here, but I feel like I don't fit in. I KNOW I don't fit in. And even if any of these people knew how to get me back to Dres land, well... I'm too afraid to ask.
I'm going to die! I'm going to be ripped up and turned into whatever these things eat! I'll be thrown into an incinerator!

Please! Don't tell anyone here! I don't even know how I got to this place! I was wandering outside Tear and sat on a stump, and the next moment I found myself in this city! Everyone is all mechanical and scary and they look at me funny! Please, I don't want to get killed!

It is said by many that the legs of Sotha Sil had secrets stored away, and these secrets would come and go as needed. To a more practical man, this means that the enchantment of the greaves changes, depending on what you are doing. As I understand it, if you are running, jumping, sneaking, or swimming, the enchantment will change.

It was on the northern edge of the district, near this house, and heavily damaged, perhaps enough for it to shift and reveal the path to power. It has been sealed within the past few days, but it seems not soon enough to stop our Overclocker friends. We must reach them before their experimentation threatens the entire city. And yet in the way stand the Watchmen.
Hm.
It might be possible to use the outages to our advantage.
Speaking.
Yes?

A conjurer thought himself wise to summon me. He thought himself less wise when I slaughtered his nearby wife. But I suppose he had the last laugh, as my soul, crystal now in form, inhabits the body of his late lover.
I despise this form. I mean, why do you have to eat food? What is food? Why are you mortals so utterly weak!
And why can I not kill myself?
Thanks for, uh, finding it.

Oh, you found it? Thank you. I think. I'll send people to retrieve it. As soon as, you know, I find people.
I have this. It does something, I think. You can have it.

It would be nice if someone found it.
It, uh, doesn't have to be intact

Yes. Carts. On rails. Without anything but magic to move them.
It, uh, didn't work. My first test run (He points to the hole in the ceiling) went too fast, jumped the track, and went flying.
You, uh? Get out a lot? If you find it would you mind telling me? It probably went somewhere in the Temple district.

Not undead, but a dwemer-based automaton that lives in the catacombs. They have a nasty tendency to repair anything they perceive as allies, which unfortunately include the standard undead. They are always passive though, unless attacked.
He's still not arrested yet, but let me tell you, that tree-hugging fetcher soon will be!
He's still not arrested yet, but let me tell you, that gear-loving fetcher soon will be!
It's planted? Excellent! I can almost smell him getting arrested, I'm shaking just thinking about that n'wah getting what's coming to him. Please, take this for your help!
It's planted? Excellent! I can almost smell him getting arrested, I'm shaking just thinking about that n'wah getting what's coming to him. Please, take this for your help!
Go to my rival's house in the western Residential District, and plant this evidence in, say, his closet or something.
Go to my rival's house in the western Residential District, and plant this evidence in, say, his dresser or something.

Just look at him, standing over there waving around how superior his "naturally grown" fabricants are. He makes me sick he does. That's why I've been plotting for the longest time. I've got this false evidence, and if I could manage to break into his house in eastern side of the Residential District, I could get him arrested and thrown out of business. But I can't leave my post. But... perhaps you could? I think both you and I agree a man like that needs to be put away.

Just look at him, standing over there waving around how superior his "mechanically enhanced" fabricants are. He makes me sick he does. That's why I've been plotting for the longest time. I've got this false evidence, and if I could manage to break into his house in eastern side of the Residential District, I could get him arrested and thrown out of business. But I can't leave my post. But... perhaps you could? I think both you and I agree a man like that needs to be put away.
She'll never like me now... Unless maybe she's into pyromaniacs?

Oh no! I forgot to rig it up to explode later!
And why is it burning! The city is made out of metal! Metal doesn't burn! What? A reward? Fine, have this, just... get out of the way!

They are all set up? You're sure? Well, I've got the detonator right here, let's hope it works.
3... 2... 1...
Place the fireworks I gave you in the chimneys around this district, so I can set them off.

I... well... She's an amazing fabricant, really! But she doesn't even know I exist. But she will! Or... she should.
I had this light show, some fire-based magical fireworks... all you know, rigged up. Sort of. I haven't gotten a chance to place them anywhere. But I saw some old chimneys on the rooftops. If someone or I or... someone, could reach them and place the fireworks in there, I could set them off, and then she'd know who I am for sure!
Say, could you be that someone? I have money!

The worst sort. They willfully and rampantly deviate from Lord Sotha Sil's designs, heedless of the cost to their souls and the consequences to those around them. They're fanatical and dangerous in their pursuit of ever-more-powerful alterations, and will go to any lengths they believe necessary to do so. I'd stay far away from them if I were you.

We believe that Lord Sotha Sil gave us these bodies as gifts, to do with what we pleased. We know that he did not personally create us, and we know that our forms are not sacred. He wants us to think. To explore. To use our right reason in pursuit of the truth. And, to do so, we must first perfect ourselves. No mind can truly be free if the body falters, so we tweak and tinker and refine ourselves further and further in pursuit of perfection.

The Overclockers are one of two major factions in the city. They believe in enlightenment and perfection by any means necessary, and are masters of mechanical and artificial enhancements. They are largely supported by craftsmen, and as such, their base is made in the Industrial District. They are constantly at war with the Abstemious due to philosophical differences.

And this connects to this, then that, and....
Perfect! The legs of god, reassembled! Do you wish to know how they work friend? They are yours, of course, for you found them. To see them work is all I need for a reward.
Oh, what a sight.

Those... that, I can't believe it! Those are the pieces of god! Long ago the Clockwork God had legs, as any mortal does. But, he knew then that such modus of transport was too lowly for him, so he removed his legs, replacing them with magical machinery by which he would float.
His left-behind-legs, still powerful, wandered off on their own, into the outer halls of his city, where they eventually split and sat for ages. But you have found all six of them! If you would, please sera, let me see them.

Indeed! Long ago the Clockwork God had legs, as any mortal does. But, he knew then that such modus of transport was too lowly for him, so he removed his legs, replacing them with magical machinery by which he would float.
His left-behind-legs, still powerful, wandered off on their own, into the outer halls of his city, where they eventually split and sat for ages. Indeed, all six of those pieces must still be out there in the outer city.
You do understand what you're asking, right?
Honor the ancestors with your heart, not with your tongue.
The powerless given voice, bonds reforged.

Ah, so the seeker-adventurer comes to fix, repair, or otherwise heal our problems yes? The Archcanon has told me of your arrival, and perhaps you shall have more success than we have. But if you are indeed to succeed, or otherwise triumph, perhaps it would be best if you were aware of the nature of the problem. And if you must be aware of, or otherwise knowledgeable, of our problems, perhaps it would be best if you knew about fabricant social dynamics.
The powerless.

I have heard. A secret transicant, slipping right past me. It is a sign of hard times on the city indeed.
Nevertheless, I thank you for restoring the Residential District's peace.

It is where many fabricants eat, drink, and love, but it has often been subject to, ah, let us call it class tension. The district was split between the prosperous and the less-so, though in recent times the feud between the two sides has escalated far more than it ever should. I believe someone is encouraging this conflict, and if you were to stop them, then the troubles of that district would return to their normal levels. Speak to the leader of the Abstemious, as she knows more than I do.

text: He he he, I've a few good memories of that place, and Aroban's a good man. Sorry, getting distracted. The center building is the home of the Abstemious, who provide alchemical, healing, and religious services here in this district. They also separate the rich and the poor. On the rich side, you have the well-known inn, the Swing of the Clock, which provides services for outlanders staying in the city.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Clockwork City, Residential District
text: Welcome, friend, to the place where most fabricants make home! The counterpart to this district is the slums, but that's on lockdown. At any rate, the Residential District is divided into two sides, the Working Sector and the Thinking Sector, or poor and rich respectively. Most interest points can be found on the Working Sector, including the Emporium, on the south end, Monan's Spa, which is that collection of buildings next to the center complex, and the House of Sehtly Wonders, at the end of the alley.
The Residential District is almost exclusively for habitation for those fabricants too wealthy to live in the slums. It has a few shops, but not much that'd interest an adventurer like yourself.

My own phrase, you understand. I hear tell that the citizens of the city often call them "Bone Stokers". They are the guardian spirits and ancestors of the fabricants born in the city. Animated by machinery and magic, forever keeping watch over the catacombs. But they are quick to anger, and if disturbed, it is often for a very serious reason. If you ever cross paths with one, I hope you are well prepared, for they are quite powerful.
Speak to them, observe them in their base, break rules if you have to. Find out what they know about the power core, if they do at all.

I am not stupid, mortal, your hideous smiling does not change that. I have researched the nature of my mortal shell, and should it die, my soul will be wiped, and readied to be put in a new fabricant vessel, and thus, not back into Oblivion.
It is a clever trap, and I wonder if the maker of this horrible metal world did not intend such failsafes for larger targets.

Indeed. They have come. Reluctantly, but nonetheless willing. Three children have new homes. Though perhaps I will have to monitor them; reluctance to accept may mean reluctance to raise. Nevertheless, you have done well. Accept these as a token of my gratitude.
I said I would. I hope you're happy.
Okay! I'll do it! But remember, whatever blood follows will on your hands!
Please! He and I were just joking around! We can't afford a baby! Have financial mercy!
I told ya I'll do what ya want, shut it already.
Oh fine, if it'll shut ya up, I'll go look at the little fetcher. The missus won't be too happy though.
Hahahah. Nah.
Yes, yes, I'm going I'm going!

Alright, fine! So I was under pressure from own parents, it's not my fault, I was drunk! 
There's no way I'm getting out of this, am I? Fine. Tell the Foremer I'll pick up... whatever gender the thing is, later.
I don't know what you're talking about!
Find the three I have requested you to find. Convince them to return to me and collect the children they requested. Do not kill them. Do not take 'no' for an answer.

Births in the Clockwork City are hard, but sometimes what comes next is harder. Three fabricants refuse to become the parents they requested to be. I have written their names and locations down on this piece of paper. Find them. Threaten them if necessary. Convince them to collect what is theirs.
Fair enough. If you want to duel, I'll be waiting.
Alright, let's hope you're a challenge. The last fabricant I wrestled had his head pop off two minutes in.
No weapons, first one to faint loses. You in, or are you out?

Rare. Quite rare. Square gears are not unusual, for the clockwork god uses them in many things, but an errant square gear, such as this, is something else. Sotha Sil prefers us to think that which turns must be round, as roundness rhymes with rolling and round things roll. But this is not the case. Roundness is relative. Turning is relative. I shall trade you this gear, for another. Perhaps in time, you will find a use for my gear, as, hopefully, I will find a use for yours.
I am no longer the archcanon, Nerevarine. As a final gift, know my real name. I am Ulanaunit, Chronography Eternity Ulanaunit. Farewell.

("Subject is resistant to shock magic, which, unlike the fire spell, is unexpected. Can't risk draining the tank, but this warrant further study.")

(Coin and drink always eases tensions, you've realized. Even a hateful drunk will at least quaff his mug of sujamma down before throwing a punch, and the dingy atmosphere grows peaceful with alcoholic comradery. You return to your table, trying not to let your satisfaction show on your face.)
("That's going to lose us a lot of coin," the scholar says. "And this isn't a town that will barter for strange trinkets.")

(Someone told you once that knowing you're certain to die was a freeing thought. They were wrong. There are more people here that you could ever expect. (Somehow, despite knowing you're going to die. You live. Years later you'll still wake up, dreaming of the corpse sea.)

("Show me how you did this.")

text: I've got a love problem.
Damn that other farmer!
Damn that other farmer!

Ah! No doubt this wandering, wondering one has come to the Shrine of the Footed seeking tales of the fable Legs of Seht! 
Well listen well, wonderwanderer, for I have much to tell.

It is the final lesson of Sotha Sil, %PCName. The only way for the world to change is for you to make it change. Every second is a decision, every minute a choice. And this is our decision, our choice. The world is going to change soon, and these changes require guidance. Decisions must be made. We feel that we can make those decisions, and so, we are leaving.

So. The heart of the machine god beats no longer. He is dead, and his pain has been eased. Perhaps he would have gone mad, perhaps not. Now the city dies, though we, the highest born, are severed from and spared from its easing. And so, we must plan.
We have you to thank, %PCName. Though our god has died, you have ended his experiment, and in doing so, have learned and taught us something valuable.

The heart beats once more, and stronger than ever. Perhaps in time Gestalt, or shall we call him Seht now, will slip to Sheogorath's Domain, but for now, the city moves smoothly once more, and our brothers and sisters walk through the street unmolested by time or other. We of the high-born, however, have other plans, and have you to thank for them.
